questions.question: In cyclic quadrilateral ABCD, angle A = 105°. Find angle C, outline why opposite angles must be supplementary, and state the exterior-angle companion theorem.
questions.expected_answer: Angle C = 180° − 105° = 75° — opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral. Why: the angle at B stands on arc ADC and the angle at D stands on arc ABC; their central angles are twice B and twice D, and those two central angles together sweep the whole 360° about the centre, so 2B + 2D = 360°, giving B + D = 180° (and likewise A + C). Companion: extending a side produces an exterior angle that makes 180° with its interior neighbour, and since the interior opposite angle also makes 180° with that neighbour, the exterior angle of a cyclic quadrilateral equals the interior opposite angle. Both theorems require all four vertices genuinely on the circle in cyclic order.

questions.question: P lies 17 units from the centre O of a circle of radius 8; the tangents from P touch at A and B and angle APB = 52°. Find the length of each tangent and the base angles of triangle PAB, with reasons.
questions.expected_answer: Tangent length: OA meets PA at 90° (tangent perpendicular to radius), so triangle OAP is right-angled at A with hypotenuse OP: PA² = 17² − 8² = 289 − 64 = 225, so PA = 15. By the two-tangent theorem PA = PB = 15 (tangents from same point; proved by RHS congruency on triangles OAP and OBP). Triangle PAB is therefore isosceles, so its base angles are equal and share 180° − 52° = 128°: angles PAB and PBA are 64° each (base angles of isosceles triangle; angle sum of triangle).

questions.question: State the tangent-chord theorem, use it to find angle ACB in the rider above (C on the major arc AB), and describe the independent cross-check that confirms the answer.
questions.expected_answer: Tangent-chord: the angle between a tangent and a chord drawn at the point of contact equals the angle subtended by that chord in the alternate segment. Angle PAB = 64° is the angle between tangent PA and chord AB, so the angle on AB from the alternate (major-arc) segment is also 64°: angle ACB = 64° — tangent-chord. Cross-check by a second road: in quadrilateral OAPB the angles at A and B are 90° each, so angle AOB = 360° − 90° − 90° − 52° = 128°; the circumference angle on the major arc is half of that, 64° — angle at centre is twice angle at circumference. Two independent theorem chains landing on 64° certify the answer.
